- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after spikes or high volatility periods; reduce forecast slope after sharp upward moves.
- Forecast mean tends to be 2–5% above true outcome, suggesting a systematic upward bias; apply downward adjustment of 1.5–3% for the first 5–7 days.
- After a true price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: if true >85, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
- Sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) — no signal to adjust for sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment were positive, expect model to overreact; if negative, expect underreaction — but in this case, no sentiment signal, so ignore sentiment-based corrections.
- Model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias: forecasts drift upward but true values often revert to lower range after initial spike — apply a “reversion buffer” rule: if forecast >85 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days; consider using 10-day moving average of true values as a baseline for early correction.
